A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe RADAb. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable, including material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 report original antibody sequence-design, computed binding-energy, and ablation results. The appendices include length-dependent results and additional antibody case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original computational results and adds binding-energy results for top-ranked generated candidates in Appendix A.7 and Table 5.

M1.justification: Structural retrieval, the ESM2/global and axial-attention/local branches, fusion, training objective, and sampling procedure remain unchanged. Figure 2's fixed-structure clarification and folding/relaxation depiction describe procedures already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SAbDab/PDB-based inverse-folding and functionality tasks, long-CDR-H3 subset, and case-study complexes. The additional ranked-candidate results remain within existing coverage; PPI retrieval is discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their comparator sets: Grafting, ProteinMPNN, ESM-IF1, Diffab-fix, and AbMPNN where applicable. Table 5 extends reporting for existing optimization baselines, with no top-k entries for Grafting. Rosetta-Fixbb remains explicitly unevaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 adds evaluation of ΔΔG-seq for the first-, second-, and third-ranked generated structures. Existing splits, eight samples per CDR, training budgets, model configurations, and original evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new ranked-candidate analysis examines the quality of the best generated structures beyond the aggregate functionality results reported in v1. Retrieval/evolutionary ablations, retrieval-count sensitivity, CDR-length analysis, and structural case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run statistics, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The sampling counts are unchanged, and the new top-ranked scores do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing table and figure results are retained. New Table 5 reports RADAb F-top1/F-top2/F-top3 values of -69.30/-55.95/-45.96 alongside baseline scores. RADAb leads the first two ranks, while Diffab-fix has the lower third-ranked value (-46.13). These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under an unchanged metric.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(8), and algorithmic formulations are unchanged. Removing v1 Appendix B's informal search-space discussion, including its 20^L illustration, does not revise the formal theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same retrieval-augmented antibody-design proposal, generative-model-agnostic claim, and performance claims. The new appendix results support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New Appendix E explains the practical motivation for sequence-only inverse folding. Appendices E–F explicitly identify potential leakage when known CDR structures guide sequence–structure co-design and discuss prospective PPI/MASIF retrieval. These add substantive applicability qualifications to the existing limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Reproducibility Statement identifying the GENTEL-lab/RADAb code repository. The implementation settings, hardware, retrieval thresholds, training budgets, and reconstruction details already present in v1 are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands discussion of the already cited RetMol and IRDiff methods. New appendix discussion adds Frey, Shanehsazzadeh, and Gainza references concerning antibody design and protein-interaction retrieval; several earlier bibliography entries are removed. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized related-work edits, adds reproducibility and acknowledgment sections, adds Appendices A.7 and E, removes the old Appendix B discussion, and renumbers retained appendix material. Author affiliations and headers change, while most main-text prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is revised to clarify fixed-backbone diffusion and subsequent folding/relaxation. Table 5 is added, Table 1 and Figure 3 are relocated, and table shading, headers, and spacing change. Existing experimental plots and case-study images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through explicit known-backbone applicability and leakage limitations, a clearer Figure 2, and code-access information. Table 5 adds useful evidence about the best generated candidates, including a third-rank exception to RADAb's lead. These are limited gains: the method, main results, and lack of wet-lab validation remain unchanged.
